meta.seoTitle: Headless CMS demo: content models, visual editor and API
meta.seoDescription: Try a headless CMS with sample data: content models, visual block editor, web and app preview, SEO checks, roles, approvals, scheduled publishing, webhooks and a JSON API. AI writing assistant included.

bar.title: Headless CMS
bar.sampleHint: Fictitious company, people, addresses, phone numbers and domains. Your changes are saved only in this browser.
bar.subtitle: Model your content, edit it in a visual editor, approve it and publish it to your website, your app and your assistant from a single panel.
bar.switched: You are now viewing the demo as {name} ({role}).
bar.storageOff: Your browser does not allow saving data: changes will be lost when you reload the page.
bar.resetBody: This deletes the entries, images, fields and publications you created or changed in this browser and loads the sample data again.
bar.resetDone: Done: the sample data was loaded again.

writer.name: Writer
writer.desc: Creates entries, edits drafts and published entries (as a draft) and sends them for review.

editor.name: Editor
editor.desc: Reviews, approves, schedules and publishes; can edit any entry.

admin.name: Administrator
admin.desc: Everything above, plus content models and webhooks.

status.liveHint: The site keeps showing the published version until you publish these changes.

page.name: Page
page.desc: Site pages (home, about us) built with blocks.

article.name: Blog article
article.desc: News, guides and announcements with date, category and cover image.
article.example: How to prepare for your lab test

location.name: Location
location.desc: Each location with address, hours, WhatsApp, photo and the services it offers.

service.name: Service
service.desc: Services with summary, self-pay rate from, preparation and image.

faq.name: FAQ
faq.desc: Questions and answers shown on the site that the assistant can cite.
faq.example: Can I change my appointment time?

home.roleLine: You are viewing the demo with the {role} role. {desc} Switch person with “View as” to try the permissions.
home.tourIntro: Each step is checked automatically when you actually do it in the demo.

model.title: 1. See how content is modeled
model.desc: Open “Content models” and review the “Location” type: fields, required and translatable. As an administrator you can add a field.

edit.title: 2. Edit the Chapinero location and watch the preview
edit.desc: Change the hours or the photo: the web and app preview updates as you type.

assistant.title: 3. Ask the writing assistant for a shorter version
assistant.desc: In the “AI assistant” tab use “Short version for the app” and apply it to the field.

publish.title: 4. Send for review, approve and publish
publish.desc: Send as Writer, switch to Editor with “View as”, approve and publish. See the webhook under “Publishing” and the JSON in the “API” tab.

rag.title: 5. Publish the FAQ and ask the site assistant
rag.desc: Publish “How do I prepare for an abdominal ultrasound?” and ask about the ultrasound in the preview: the assistant cites the published answer.

home.truthTitle: What is real in this demo

browser.title: Works in your browser:
browser.desc: models, entries, visual editor, preview, SEO checks, roles, approvals, scheduling, versions and the API JSON. It is saved in this browser.

ai.title: Real AI:
ai.desc: the writing assistant sends the text to the KopTup backend, which calls a language model.

simulated.title: Simulated:
simulated.desc: webhooks (nothing is sent), the .example domains, the image CDN and the site assistant (keyword search over the published FAQs).

project.title: In your project:
project.desc: we implement it with your content model, your site and your app, permissions enforced on the server and the integrations you need.

api.title: Delivery API
api.subtitle: This is how your site, your app or your assistant reads the content. Change the filters and look at the JSON: it comes from this demo's data.
api.copyFailed: We could not copy: select the text and copy it manually.
api.snippetComment: the publish webhook revalidates this tag
api.point1: Without preview, the API only delivers published content; drafts never leave.
api.point2: If a translation is missing, it delivers the Spanish text and flags it in “localeFallback”.
api.point3: Images come with alt text, size and focal point so each channel can crop them.
api.simulated: API simulated in your browser with this demo's data (.example domains). In your project the CMS server serves it, with REST or GraphQL as you need.
api.notPublished: This entry has no published version: the API responds 404. With preview (and its token) you would see the draft.

history.note: Changes are saved automatically in this browser; “Save version”, sending, approving and publishing create a point in the history.

ai.realNote: Real AI: the selected text is sent to the KopTup backend, which processes it with a language model. Do not include personal data.
ai.emptySource: This field is empty in the selected language.
ai.tooShort: The text is already short (fewer than 12 words).
ai.copyFailed: We could not copy the text.
ai.uses: {n, plural, =0 {You have not used the AI in this visit yet.} one {You used the AI # time in this visit.} other {You used the AI # times in this visit.}}

ai.noTargets: This entry has no text fields to work on with the AI.

errors.network: We could not reach the AI server. Check your connection or try again later; the rest of the demo keeps working.
errors.timeout: The AI took too long to respond. Try again with a shorter text.
errors.notConfigured: The AI assistant is not configured on this server (the model key is missing). The rest of the demo works the same.
errors.rateLimited: You reached the request limit for now. Wait a few minutes and try again.
errors.invalid: The server did not accept that text. Try a longer or different text.
errors.server: The AI service responded with an error. Try again in a moment.

models.title: Content models
models.subtitle: In a headless CMS the content is structured: each type defines its fields and each channel (web, app, assistant) applies its own design.
models.adminOnly: Only Administrators can change the models. Use “View as” to try it.
models.fieldRemoved: Field removed from the model and its entries.
models.headlessNote: The demo's base fields cannot be deleted; fields you add show up in the editor, in the preview (additional information) and in the API JSON.
models.idTaken: A field with the ID {id} already exists.
models.requiredWarn: Existing entries of this type cannot be sent or published until they fill in this field.
models.fieldAdded: Field “{name}” added: it already shows up in the editor and the API.

publishing.title: Publishing
publishing.subtitle: Editorial queue, scheduled publications and notifications (webhooks) to your channels.
publishing.blocked: It has pending fields: open it to fix them.
publishing.writerNote: As a Writer you can see the queue, but approving and publishing belong to Editors. Use “View as” to switch person.

app.name: App
app.desc: Tells the app to refresh its content.

assistant.name: Assistant
assistant.desc: Reindexes the FAQs the assistant can cite.

publishing.hookOff: Webhook disabled: that channel will no longer be notified.
publishing.adminOnly: Only Administrators can enable, disable or resend webhooks.
publishing.deliveriesEmpty: No deliveries yet. Publish or unpublish an entry to see them here.
publishing.simulatedNote: Simulated: the demo sends nothing to the internet and the domains are .example. In your project, publishing calls your site's revalidation, your app and your assistant's reindexing.

rolesView.title: Roles and permissions
rolesView.subtitle: Three sample people with different roles. Switch person and try: buttons and actions follow these permissions.
rolesView.current: You are viewing as this person

rolesView.note: In the demo, each action's logic checks the permission again (hiding buttons is not enough). In your project, permissions are enforced on the CMS server and can be integrated with your company's sign-in if you need it.
